subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw core add a narrow safe fallback to read for known binary document formats, or should this remain only tool guidance and broader document-ingest work?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the token-waste path, but AGENTS.md and VISION.md make fallback behavior and core document parsing product-scope decisions rather than purely mechanical fixes.

options.title: Add narrow read fallback
options.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable unsupported-binary-document message for known PDF/Office formats and does not parse them inline.

options.title: Keep read text/image-only by policy
options.body: Only update tool guidance and rely on the existing pdf tool or future document tools, accepting that unsupported binary reads can still be attempted.

options.title: Fold into broader document ingestion
options.body: Track this under provider-native/document attachment work and require security and dependency review before adding broader parsing behavior.

recommendation.title: Add narrow read fallback
recommendation.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable unsupported-binary-document message for known PDF/Office formats and does not parse them inline.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent current-main history signal on the read-tool files that would need the fallback.
